sourcedFrom: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The Model 1300 field strips to two pieces: magazine cap off, barrel forward off the magazine tube, cap straight back on. Winchester's book then publishes a Complete Disassembly for cleaning the action — trigger guard group out on one pin, slide arms and breech bolt out of the receiver, firing pin out of the bolt — and that is the Deep Clean lane below. One fact about your gun decides part of it: the gauge. On a 12 gauge the slide arms and bolt come out the front of the receiver together; on a 20 gauge the bolt will not pass the front, so the slide arms come off the bridge first and the bolt drops out through the trigger guard opening. The book stops at the firing pin and forbids going further.

steps.title: Cycle the tube empty, then feel the magazine entry
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction, put the safety on safe and close the action. Hold the disconnector release button in to free the slide, then run the forearm through complete strokes until every shell in the magazine has gone through the chamber and out of the ejection port, and leave the action open. Then put your index finger into the magazine entry. A tube magazine is a blind hole: a shell held back by the cartridge cutoff looks exactly like an empty tube, and only your finger can tell the difference.
steps.prose: The book also publishes a second route: gun upside down, carrier pushed down, and the cartridge cutoff on the inside-right of the ejection port pressed to release one shell at a time.
steps.quote: Using your index finger, feel the entry of the magazine to make sure there are no longer any shells in the magazine.
steps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Unloading Procedures, step 6 (printed p.12)
steps.warn: Feel the magazine entry. Do not judge a tube by eye.

steps.title: The disconnector release button opens the action without dropping the hammer
steps.action: The button behind the trigger guard on the LEFT side unlocks the slide when the action is closed. Push it up and pull the forearm back and the action opens, but the hammer stays where it is. You will use it at the start of every strip below, because the only other way to unlock a closed Model 1300 is to pull the trigger. Find it by feel now, with the gun empty.
steps.prose: It is the same button you held in to unload the tube.
steps.quote: Depress the disconnector release button, found behind the trigger guard on the left side (Figure 5) to unlock the action without releasing the hammer.
steps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Initial Assembly/Takedown — TAKEDOWN, step 1 (printed p.10)

steps.title: Safety on safe: button fully to the right, no red showing
steps.action: The safety is a cross-bolt button just forward of the trigger in the trigger guard. On safe is the button pushed fully to the RIGHT, so the red band on the left side is hidden; off safe is pushed fully to the left with a large red band showing. Every stage of the strip below starts with it on safe. Check it by feel and position as well as colour.
steps.prose: Winchester warns that the red band can be worn away by time, weather and cleaning agents, so its absence alone does not prove the gun is on safe.
steps.caution: Do not rely on the red band alone; it can wear off.
steps.quote: “ON SAFE” — The safety button is pushed fully to the right. The red band on the left side is not showing.
steps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Operation of the Safety (printed p.8)

steps.title: Read the barrel: 12 or 20 gauge decides how the bolt comes out
steps.action: Read the marking on the left side of the barrel before you go any further. It tells you the gauge and the ammunition this gun takes, and Winchester tells you to use exactly that and nothing else. It also decides your Deep Clean: the slide and breech bolt come out one way on a 12 gauge and a different way on a 20 gauge, and the book prints the two procedures under separate headings. Know which gun you are holding before you start the strip.
steps.prose: All current 12 and 20 gauge Model 1300s, the book says, have a 3 inch chamber.
steps.caution: The barrel marking decides the gauge and the ammunition.
steps.quote: MAKE SURE YOU USE ONLY THE EXACT AMMUNITION/GAUGE AS LISTED ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE BARREL.
steps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Ammunition (printed p.4)

steps.title: Action open, safety on safe
steps.action: With the gun unloaded, press the disconnector release button and open the action, then put the safety on safe. Look for the red band to be hidden. Taking the barrel off with the action open is how Winchester's takedown is written, and it lets the bolt lugs clear the barrel extension.
steps.prose: Opening the action this way leaves the hammer cocked, which is what the trigger group removal in Deep Clean needs anyway.
steps.quote: Open the action and place the safety in the “on safe” position. (The red warning band must not be visible.)
steps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Initial Assembly/Takedown — TAKEDOWN, step 2 (printed p.10)

steps.title: Magazine cap off, with the tube pointed away from you
steps.action: Point the end of the magazine tube in a safe direction, away from your face and anyone else, and unscrew the magazine cap. The magazine spring and plug are held in the tube only by a friction-type retainer, not by the cap, so they should stay put — but if the retainer has been disturbed they can come out with force. The mistake is unscrewing the cap with the tube aimed at yourself.
steps.prose: The cap is the only thing holding the barrel on; there is no barrel nut or screw.
steps.quote: With the magazine pointed in a safe direction, unscrew and remove the magazine cap. Be careful, the magazine spring and magazine plug are retained by a friction-type retainer.
steps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Initial Assembly/Takedown — TAKEDOWN, step 3 (printed p.10)
steps.warn: Keep the magazine tube pointed away from you and others when the cap comes off.

steps.title: Barrel forward off the receiver and the magazine tube
steps.action: Grip the barrel just ahead of the barrel bracket with one hand and the buttstock with the other. Pull the barrel forward to draw the barrel extension out of the receiver, then slide the barrel bracket off the end of the magazine tube. It should come with steady pressure. If it will not move, the action is not fully open and the bolt lugs are still in the barrel extension — open the action, do not pull harder.
steps.prose: The rotary bolt's lugs lock straight into the barrel extension, not into the receiver, which is why an open action is all it takes to free the barrel.
steps.quote: Pull the barrel to disengage it from the receiver. Slide the barrel bracket off the magazine. Do not use excessive force.
steps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Initial Assembly/Takedown — TAKEDOWN, step 4 (printed p.10)

steps.title: Magazine cap straight back on, at least three turns
steps.action: As soon as the barrel is off, screw the magazine cap back onto the tube and hand-tighten it at least three full turns. With the barrel gone, the cap is the only thing keeping the friction retainer, spring and plug from being knocked out of the tube while you clean. Hand tight is the book's figure; it does not call for a tool.
steps.prose: If you are going on to the Deep Clean, the cap comes off again there — the bolt cannot come out with it on.
steps.quote: Immediately replace the magazine cap and hand tighten at least three turns.
steps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Initial Assembly/Takedown — TAKEDOWN, step 4 (printed p.10)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You should have two pieces on the bench: the barrel, and the receiver and stock with the forearm and magazine tube, the cap back on. That is Winchester's takedown, and it opens the bore to a rod from the chamber end. Deep Clean goes on into the book's Complete Disassembly — the trigger guard group, the slide arms and breech bolt, and the firing pin — and walks the bore, choke tube and receiver cleaning that strip opens up.
steps.prose: The book's own reassembly for this level is the barrel back over the tube, the slot in the barrel lined up with the ejector, then the cap hand tight.
steps.quote: The Model 1300 breaks down for easy cleaning and storage.
steps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — General Operation (printed p.3)

deepSteps.title: Eye protection on — and the book's limit, stated up front
deepSteps.action: Put on eye protection before you go further; several parts below are under spring tension. Winchester opens its Complete Disassembly with a hard limit: nothing beyond what the book explains and shows. That limit is the firing pin out of the breech bolt, at the end of this lane. Lay out a clean surface and somewhere for the small parts before you start.
deepSteps.prose: The book says this can be done in the field, but that there are small parts involved.
deepSteps.quote: WEAR EYE PROTECTION AT ALL TIMES. NEVER DISASSEMBLE BEYOND WHAT IS EXPLAINED AND SHOWN IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly (printed p.21)
deepSteps.warn: Eye protection on. Parts below are under spring tension.

deepSteps.title: Cock the hammer and put the safety on safe
deepSteps.action: With the gun confirmed empty, slide the forearm fully rearward and then fully forward. That cocks the hammer, which is the state the trigger guard group must come out in and go back in. Then put the safety on safe. Lay the gun trigger-guard-up on something that will not mark the receiver or stock.
deepSteps.prose: If the barrel is off, keep the magazine cap on for this stage so the spring retainer stays put.
deepSteps.quote: Cycle the action by sliding the forearm rearward and then forward. This puts the hammer in the cocked position. Place the safety in the “on safe” position.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — REMOVAL OF THE TRIGGER GUARD GROUP, step 2 (printed p.21)

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard pin out from the LEFT side
deepSteps.action: Push the trigger guard pin out from the LEFT side of the receiver — the side away from the ejection port — with a pushing tool smaller than the pin that will not mar the finish. Push until you can grip the pin with your fingers, then pull it the rest of the way. Direction matters: the book drives it out from the left and puts it back from the right. Keep a firm grip on both the tool and the gun while you push.
deepSteps.prose: Use a punch small enough to pass completely through the hole, or the tool will damage the hole on the way.
deepSteps.caution: Out from the left, back in from the right.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the trigger guard pin by pushing it out from the LEFT side of the receiver, the side opposite the ejection port.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — REMOVAL OF THE TRIGGER GUARD GROUP, step 5 (printed p.21)

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard group up and back out of the receiver
deepSteps.action: With the pin out, tilt the rear of the trigger guard group up and draw it rearward out of the receiver. It is an up-and-back motion, not a straight lift, because its front tabs sit in slots at the magazine throat. Keep the group cocked and set it down flat. The trigger guard group must come out before the bolt assembly does.
deepSteps.prose: With it out you can see up into the bottom of the receiver.
deepSteps.quote: With the pin removed, lift the trigger guard group out of the receiver by lifting upward and pulling rearward (Figure 13).
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — REMOVAL OF THE TRIGGER GUARD GROUP, step 7 (printed p.22)

deepSteps.title: 12 gauge: slide arms and bolt out the FRONT together
deepSteps.action: 12 gauge only. With the barrel and trigger guard group out and the magazine cap OFF, slide the forearm, slide arms and breech bolt assembly forward together and out of the front of the receiver, still joined at the slide arm bridge. Expect resistance as the bolt passes the ejection port — that is the ejector spring bearing on the bolt. Work it past gently; a hard pull is what bends an ejector.
deepSteps.prose: The cap has to be off because the forearm and slide arms leave over the end of the magazine tube.
deepSteps.caution: 12 gauge only. A 20 gauge bolt will not come out the front.
deepSteps.quote: With the action slide arms still attached to the slide arm bridge, simultaneously slide both assemblies forward and out of the front of the receiver. Note that as the breech bolt assembly passes by the ejection port, there may be some resistance from the ejector spring. Carefully work it past the resistance.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — DISASSEMBLY OF THE SLIDE AND BREECH BOLT (12 GAUGE ONLY), step 2 (printed p.22)

deepSteps.title: 20 gauge: slide arms off the bridge, bolt out through the bottom
deepSteps.action: 20 gauge only. The bolt will not pass out of the front of the receiver on a 20 gauge, so do not try. With the barrel and trigger guard group out and the magazine cap off, disengage the slide arms from the slide arm bridge first. Then take the slide arms out through the front of the receiver, and bring the bolt slide assembly out downward through the opening the trigger guard group left.
deepSteps.prose: Winchester gives the reason itself: the 20 gauge bolt will not extract through the front of the receiver as it does on the 12 gauge.
deepSteps.caution: 20 gauge only. Forcing the bolt out of the front is the mistake.
deepSteps.quote: You must disengage the slide arms from the slide arm bridge. Remove the slide arms through the front of the receiver. Remove the bolt slide assembly through the trigger guard group opening.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — DISASSEMBLY OF THE SLIDE AND BREECH BOLT (20 GAUGE ONLY), step 2 (printed p.22)

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out — keep a finger on it
deepSteps.action: Hold the breech bolt assembly flat side up and push the rear of the firing pin forward with your forefinger, and keep it there. With your other hand tilt the front of the slide arm bridge, move it slightly forward and lift, so its curved tongue comes out of the groove in the firing pin; the bridge is now free of the bolt slide. The firing pin is under spring tension and will snap out of the rear of the bolt the moment your finger lets go. Let it out slowly into your hand, over a bench.
deepSteps.prose: Either end of the firing pin spring can go back on first, so there is nothing to mark.
deepSteps.quote: The firing pin is under spring tension and will snap out the rear of the breech bolt when your forefinger releases it. Control the pin as you remove the firing pin and spring.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — REMOVAL OF THE FIRING PIN, step 2 (printed p.23)
deepSteps.warn: The firing pin is spring-launched. Control it or lose it.

deepSteps.title: The published strip ends here
deepSteps.action: Stop. Winchester says no further dismantling is necessary or recommended for cleaning, and that going further than the parts layout it prints may void the warranty. The trigger guard group's own parts, the extractor, the ejector and the magazine spring retainer all stay where they are. A repair that needs more goes to a Winchester authorized service centre or a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.prose: The sentence points to "Figure 11 shown on page 20"; the parts layout on page 20 is printed as Figure 12. It is quoted here as the book prints it.
deepSteps.quote: For cleaning purposes no further dismantling is necessary or recommended. Do not disassemble your Model 1300 further than shown in Figure 11 shown on page 20. Doing so may void your warranty.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — after REMOVAL OF THE FIRING PIN (printed p.23)
deepSteps.warn: No disassembly beyond the firing pin.

no.q: For cleaning purposes no further dismantling is necessary or recommended. Do not disassemble your Model 1300 further than shown in Figure 11 shown on page 20. Doing so may void your warranty.
no.src: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — after REMOVAL OF THE FIRING PIN (printed p.23)

deepSteps.title: Wipe out the inside of the receiver
deepSteps.action: This is what the Complete Disassembly is for. With the trigger guard group and the bolt assembly both out, the receiver is open top and bottom: wipe out the grit, moisture and dried oil that collect along the bottom and in the slide arm tracks. A pump gun takes in dirt and water through the ejection port every time it is worked in the field. Dried oil plus dust is what makes the forearm feel tight.
deepSteps.prose: A tight action when working the forearm is the symptom the book names, and a thorough cleaning is the first thing it asks you to try.
deepSteps.quote: With both the trigger guard group and bolt assembly removed, it is easy to wipe out any debris or moisture that sometimes accumulates in the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — REMOVAL OF THE TRIGGER GUARD GROUP (printed p.21)

deepSteps.title: Bore: solvent and a brass brush, pushed all the way through
deepSteps.action: Run a snug patch through from the receiver end first, then a solvent-wet patch for ordinary powder residue. For heavy fouling, dip or spray a brass bore brush with solvent and scrub the chamber and bore. Push the brush completely out of the muzzle before drawing it back, or the bristles fold and break off. On a WinChoke barrel the choke tube must be IN while you brush — a loose bristle in the choke threads makes the tube hard to fit and remove.
deepSteps.prose: The book says a normal amount of powder residue is expected and is not serious.
deepSteps.caution: WinChoke barrel: no brass brush unless a choke tube is installed.
deepSteps.quote: If fouling should become heavy, it can be removed with a brass bore brush. Dip or spray the brush with solvent and scrub the chamber and bore until the fouling is removed. To prevent brass bristles from breaking off, the brush should be pushed completely through the bore before being withdrawn.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — CLEANING PROCEDURES, step 2 (printed p.26)

deepSteps.title: Dry the bore, one oiled patch, then look for a patch left behind
deepSteps.action: Wipe the bore dry, then pass one lightly oiled patch through for preservation. Then look through the barrel and into the chamber for a patch that came off the tip. In a shotgun bore a loose patch can sit against the wall unseen, and a patch left in the barrel is an obstruction. Look through from both ends against a light.
deepSteps.prose: Do this before the choke tube goes back in so nothing hides behind the constriction.
deepSteps.quote: INSPECT THE BARREL AND CHAMBER. MAKE CERTAIN THAT NO PATCHES HAVE BEEN INADVERTENTLY LEFT IN THEM. REMOVE ANY THAT REMAIN.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — CLEANING PROCEDURES, step 6 (printed p.26)
deepSteps.warn: A patch left in the barrel is a bore obstruction.

deepSteps.title: WinChoke threads: clean and oil them every time
deepSteps.action: If your barrel is marked WinChoke, take the tube out with the WinChoke spanner, turning it counterclockwise, and finish by hand. Clean the threads inside the muzzle and on the tube with solvent and a small soft brush, wipe them clean and leave a thin film of oil on both. Screw the tube back in by hand, tapered end first and knurled end out, and seat it firmly with the spanner without forcing it. Never fire the gun with the tube out.
deepSteps.prose: Skipping the threads is how a tube becomes difficult to remove from the barrel.
deepSteps.quote: The threads of the choke tube and the internal threads of the barrel should be cleaned after each use and before the installation of a tube.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — WinChoke Choke Tube System — SPECIAL CARE OF CHOKE TUBES AND CHOKE TUBE THREADS, step 2 (printed p.16)
deepSteps.warn: Never fire this shotgun without the WinChoke tube installed.

deepSteps.title: Oil the marked points — a light film, no more
deepSteps.action: Oil goes on the points the book marks: the bolt and its lugs, the firing pin, the ejector and the magazine tube. Put on a few drops of quality light oil and wipe it down to a film. Excess oil in the receiver runs down into the stock wood and softens it, and in cold weather it thickens and slows the action. Wipe the exposed metal with a clean rag and take off the fingerprints, where moisture collects.
deepSteps.prose: Winchester's oiling points are drawn in its Figure 2, under Initial Cleaning/Oiling.
deepSteps.quote: Avoid applying too much oil. Only a light film is necessary. Excessive oil should be wiped off, especially in cold weather.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Initial Cleaning/Oiling (printed p.8)

deepSteps.title: Reassembly order: bolt in BEFORE the trigger guard group
deepSteps.action: The bolt assembly, slide arms and forearm go back into the receiver before the trigger guard group, every time. With the hammer cocked and the safety on safe, hold the group at about 45 degrees, hook its front tabs into the slots at the magazine throat, and swing it down until it lies flush; moving the forearm can help it drop in. The pin goes back from the RIGHT side and should slide in without much force. If it resists, take the group out and start again.
deepSteps.prose: The book is plain that the bolt cannot be installed once the trigger guard group is in.
deepSteps.quote: Installing the bolt assembly after the trigger guard group is installed should not be attempted.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Complete Disassembly — REINSTALLATION OF THE TRIGGER GUARD GROUP (printed p.25)
deepSteps.warn: Bolt first, trigger guard group second. Never force it.

deepSteps.title: After heavy use, the action goes to a gunsmith
deepSteps.action: The strip above is the whole of what Winchester publishes for an owner. After long periods of heavy use, the book sends the action to a qualified gunsmith to be taken further apart for professional cleaning and lubrication. That is the deeper level — the parts left inside the trigger guard group and the receiver — and it is not an owner job.
deepSteps.prose: For a gun that shoots a few boxes a season, the strip and cleaning above is the maintenance.
deepSteps.quote: After extended periods of heavy use, your gun should be taken to a qualified gunsmith to have the action disassembled for professional cleaning and lubrication.
deepSteps.cite: Winchester® Model 1300 Owner’s Manual — UNKNOWN — no edition statement; the cover prints AO0504/04441 — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — OTHER CLEANING SUGGESTIONS (printed p.27)

cleaning.name: BARREL, BORE & CHOKE
tasks: Rod and snug patch in from the receiver end, run back and forth
Solvent-wet patch for ordinary powder residue
Brass brush with solvent for heavy fouling, pushed completely through before it is withdrawn
Do not use a brass brush in a WinChoke barrel unless a choke tube is installed
Wipe the bore dry, then one lightly oiled patch
⚠ Look through the barrel and chamber for a patch left behind, and remove it
WinChoke tube out with the spanner; clean and lightly oil the threads in the barrel and on the tube
Never fire the shotgun without the WinChoke tube installed

cleaning.name: RECEIVER, BOLT & TRIGGER GUARD GROUP
tasks: Wipe debris, moisture and dried oil out of the receiver
Wipe the bolt, its lugs and the bolt face
Clean the firing pin and its spring; either end of the spring goes on first
A few drops of light oil on the bolt, lugs, firing pin, ejector and magazine tube, then wipe to a film
Never pour oil into the receiver — it drains into the wood and softens it
Do not take the trigger guard group apart; the book stops at the firing pin

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Keep the magazine tube pointed away from you and others whenever the cap is off
The spring and plug sit behind a friction retainer — wear eye protection if the plug is being changed
Magazine cap back on hand tight, at least three full turns, whenever the barrel is on

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STOCK
tasks: Wipe the receiver, forearm and barrel metal with a clean rag and remove finger marks
Light film of oil on the metal after weather or handling
Wipe wood surfaces with a soft cloth
Camouflage and Dura-Touch finishes: no solvents — light oil or a damp cloth with mild dish soap, keeping water out of the action
Store dry, out of reach of children, ammunition stored separately

reassembly: Fit the firing pin spring over the firing pin, either end first, and insert the pin and spring into the rear opening of the bolt slide, pin end first.

Push the knob end of the firing pin in until the space between the grooved knob and the flange is centred in the round hole in the bolt slide, drop the slide arm bridge's curved tongue into that space, and release slowly so the flange draws the tongue rearward.

12 gauge: engage the slide arm bridge in the matching cuts on the slide arms, start the forearm onto the magazine tube with the cap off, and guide the slide arms and bolt into the front of the receiver, sliding them fully rearward.

20 gauge: with the trigger guard group out, put the bolt assembly up into the receiver through the trigger guard opening, bolt face and extractor toward the muzzle and slide arm bridge facing down; holding it there, insert the slide arm bars and connect them to the bridge.

With the hammer cocked and the safety on safe, turn the gun bottom-up, hold the trigger guard group at about 45 degrees, engage its front tabs in the slots at the magazine throat, and rotate it in until it lies parallel with the receiver — never force it, and never fit the bolt after it.
Push the trigger guard pin in from the RIGHT side (the ejection port side) until it is flush on both sides; it should pass with little force. If it resists, take the group out and start again.

Open the action slightly, present the barrel over and in line with the magazine tube, guide the barrel bracket over the tube and the barrel extension into the receiver with the barrel slot aligned with the ejector, and slide it rearward until it seats.
Screw the magazine cap on and hand-tighten at least three full turns.
Confirm the safety is on safe and wipe the outside down.
fncheck: With the shotgun unloaded and no ammunition on the bench, look through the bore from both ends against a light and confirm no patch is left in it. Confirm the magazine cap is hand tight with at least three full turns and the barrel does not move in the receiver. Work the forearm through several full strokes: it should run smoothly to both ends and the bolt should close fully. Press the disconnector release button with the action closed and confirm it unlocks the slide. Work the safety both ways and confirm the red band shows only with the button pushed to the left. On a WinChoke barrel, confirm the tube is in and firmly seated. Leave the safety on safe. Winchester says never to test the gun's function with live ammunition.
